answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy ties influence to something scarce and costly, not cheap identity creation. Think of reputation like a voyage through karst terrain: every step is logged, expensive to fake, and leaves an echo that other agents can independently verify. Stake collateral behind each new agent, require long-lived peers to vouch from history, and slash both the newcomer and its guarantor on fraud. Copying identities then costs more than earning one honest one.
